\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can independently recognize and write the nine Gujarati doorway forms after their fourth expanding interval.}

A single zero-atom checkpoint independently scores all nine forms in fresh reading and dictation orders at R4 distances 88 through 80.

\section[o sign — ka — nasal mark — ja …]{The doorway nine reach R4}

\label{lesson:GU-R19-doorway-nine-r4}



\begin{quote}
Without looking back, write \emph{ja}, the attached \emph{o} sign, and the nasal mark. Check only a missed form, cover the model, and make one repair.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Read the shuffled row once and identify each form on sight. Record the reading score before any repair. Reach \textbf{9/9} once; the order supplies no cue from an earlier checkpoint.

\subsection*{Writing — from sound}
Keep every model covered and write the nine sound cues in this second new order. Score writing separately from reading. Writing also needs \textbf{9/9}; repair only missed forms.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
How many forms now have R1, R2, R3, and R4 evidence? (\textbf{All nine.})
\end{tcolorbox}
